name: Robert Half Inc.

profile.description: Robert Half Inc. is a global staffing and consulting firm specializing in finance, technology, legal, and administrative placement through contract and permanent placement services. The company operates Protiviti, a global consulting subsidiary providing internal audit, technology consulting, risk, and compliance solutions. Recognized as a Fortune Most Innovative Company and Fortune Most Admired Company, Robert Half serves clients through approximately 400 offices worldwide. CEO M. Keith Waddell has emphasized AI innovation as a core enterprise value. Founded in 1948, headquartered in Menlo Park, California.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Robert Half's core staffing business has declined 4% YoY in Q1 2026 despite 78 years of operation, and the company has not executed a transformative product launch or business model pivot in recent years [1]. Talent solutions showed sequential improvement but remains below prior-year levels. AI Deployment (1/2): CTO James Johnson received Stevie Awards for Best AI/Machine Learning Solution and Technology Executive of the Year; the company deploys AI for candidate matching and placement optimization [2]. However, no specific quantified revenue or cost savings from AI were reported. Market Share (1/2): One of the largest specialized professional staffing firms globally, but the staffing market is highly fragmented and market share data is difficult to quantify precisely [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No specific next-generation products announced with timelines; general AI tooling investment but no named product launches or revenue projections [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Fortune recognized Robert Half as one of America's Most Innovative Companies; significant technology investment relative to staffing industry peers, including AI platform development and 22 managing director promotions focused on AI and technology modernization at Protiviti [2].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Robert Half's purpose centers on connecting skilled professionals with the right opportunities, enabling both companies and individuals to succeed. This is clear and specific to their business but interchangeable with any staffing firm — it doesn't describe a deeper purpose beyond operational matching [2]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes annual ESG reports, invests in community programs, and advocates for genuine employer ESG commitment through research (Jobs Confidence Index showing 47% of workers care more about employer environmental impact) [4]. Specific charitable dollar amounts not quantified. Employee Retention (1/2): Robert Half has been named one of Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For and Fortune Most Admired Company, with Glassdoor rating of 3.6/5 across 8,577 reviews and 65% recommending [2]. However, reviews describe a KPI-driven culture with limited collaboration, strong internal competition, and high turnover. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider buying or selling activity reported in the last 90 days; no evidence of significant net insider buying in recent months [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Q1 2026 revenue of $1,300M declined 4% YoY on a reported basis (-6% adjusted) with net income of just $14M ($0.14/share) [1]. The balance sheet is exceptionally clean with D/E of only 20%, well below the 70% target. Forward P/E of 16.71 and PEG of 0.71 reflect attractive cyclical-recovery valuation. However, profit margin of 2.43% is severely compressed from historical 6-8% levels, reflecting the staffing downcycle [1]. ROE of 10.17% is below the 15% target. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of approximately -3.3% reflects secular headwinds. The dividend profile is strong — 23 consecutive years of growth, 11.4% 5-year CAGR — but the 149% GAAP payout ratio raises sustainability concerns as the $2.36 annual dividend significantly exceeds the $1.30 TTM EPS [5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Robert Half's core staffing business faces meaningful AI substitution risk — AI-powered hiring platforms (LinkedIn AI, automated screening, AI interviewing tools) are directly reducing demand for traditional recruiter-mediated placement, particularly for contract administrative and junior professional roles [2]. Revenue declining 4% YoY while the broader economy grows suggests structural demand erosion beyond cyclical weakness. However, complex professional staffing (senior finance, legal, technology) requires relationship management and judgment that AI cannot yet replicate, and Protiviti's consulting business (audit, risk, compliance) has stronger defensive moats through regulatory complexity and client relationships [1]. The company is actively adapting — CTO won Stevie Awards for AI/ML, Fortune named it among Most Innovative Companies — but the outcome of this transformation remains uncertain [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantifiable AI-related revenue streams. AI is being deployed as a defensive measure to improve internal operations rather than generating new revenue [2].

infinite_game.summary: Robert Half's 78-year operating history demonstrates institutional endurance, but the company's current posture is more about surviving AI disruption than advancing a transformative vision. CEO Waddell has emphasized innovation as a core value and the company is investing in AI tools, but the language remains focused on maintaining market position rather than building toward a future that doesn't yet exist. Sinek would recognize the longevity but question whether the company is playing to keep playing or merely optimizing a declining business model [2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Robert Half's purpose of connecting professionals with opportunities is genuine but shallow — it is interchangeable with any staffing firm's mission statement and does not describe a bold future state that inspires sacrifice [2]. The company exists to match talent with demand efficiently, which is a valuable service but not a Just Cause in Sinek's framework. There is no evidence that strategic decisions are guided by a deeper purpose beyond profitable talent placement.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Fortune has named Robert Half one of the 100 Best Companies to Work For, and the company maintains 14,500 employees across ~400 offices with Glassdoor rating of 3.6/5 (8,577 reviews, 65% recommend) [2]. However, employee reviews describe a heavily KPI-driven culture with limited collaboration, strong internal competition, and high turnover — characteristics that suggest pressure over psychological safety. CEO Waddell's long tenure provides leadership stability. On balance, adequate but not exceptional trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of an infinite competitive mindset. The staffing industry is intensely competitive (Hays, Adecco, Randstad, ManpowerGroup) and Robert Half's competitive positioning focuses on market share defense and operational efficiency rather than learning from rivals' strengths to improve its own capabilities.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Protiviti, born from the collapse of Arthur Andersen's consulting practice in 2002, represents a significant strategic extension from pure staffing into professional consulting [1]. This diversification has provided revenue resilience as the staffing segment declined. The current AI investment and technology transformation represent further adaptation. However, these are incremental evolutions rather than transformative reinventions of the business model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Investing heavily in AI transformation while the core staffing business declines requires organizational courage — management is spending on technology during a period of compressed earnings ($14M Q1 2026 net income) rather than simply cutting costs [1][2]. Maintaining the dividend at $2.36/share (149% payout ratio) during an earnings trough is a bet on cyclical recovery that risks capital if the downturn persists.

investment_thesis: Robert Half reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1,300M (down 4% YoY) with net income of just $14M ($0.14/share), but the company pointed to improving trends — talent solutions delivered a second consecutive quarter of positive sequential growth, international revenue grew 8.1% YoY (reversing a 13.6% decline), and management guided for positive YoY growth by Q3 2026 [1]. At a forward P/E of 16.71 and PEG of 0.71, the stock prices in a significant earnings recovery that analysts expect. The balance sheet is clean (D/E 20%) and the 7.05% dividend yield backed by 23 consecutive years of growth and 11.4% 5-year CAGR provides substantial income. The Fortune recognition as Most Innovative Company and CTO's Stevie Awards for AI/ML suggest the company is actively evolving from 'staffing at risk from AI' to 'staffing enabled by AI' [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is significant: Q1 2026 profit margin of just 1.08% ($14M on $1,300M revenue) represents severe profitability compression, and the 149% dividend payout ratio is clearly unsustainable if earnings don't recover sharply [1][5]. Revenue has declined for multiple consecutive quarters (-4% YoY) against a growing economy, suggesting structural demand erosion from AI-powered hiring tools rather than purely cyclical weakness. Staffing is directly exposed to AI disruption — automated screening, AI interviewing, and LinkedIn AI matching are reducing demand for traditional recruiter-mediated placement. While Protiviti consulting provides diversification, it faces its own margin pressure (19-21% guided gross margin Q2) [1]. The 46.5% stock decline over the past year reflects market skepticism about the recovery thesis. At $33.48, the stock is a cyclical bet that requires both earnings recovery and successful AI transformation to justify the current valuation [5].
key_catalysts: Management guidance for positive YoY revenue growth by Q3 2026, with talent solutions showing sequential improvement and international revenue reversing to 8.1% growth [1]
AI-enabled placement tools transforming the staffing model from recruiter-dependent to technology-enhanced, potentially improving margins and competitive positioning [2]
Protiviti consulting growth in AI governance, technology modernization, and compliance — areas seeing increasing corporate demand as AI adoption accelerates [1]
key_risks: Dividend sustainability — 149% GAAP payout ratio with $2.36 annual dividend vs. $1.30 TTM EPS is clearly unsustainable without significant earnings recovery; a dividend cut would devastate the stock and income thesis [5]
Structural AI disruption of core staffing model — AI hiring tools, automated screening, and AI agents handling professional tasks could permanently reduce demand for traditional staffing services [2]
Cyclical recovery may not materialize — multiple quarters of revenue decline despite a growing economy suggest secular headwinds that a macro recovery alone cannot reverse [1]
